ground_truth_rationale: The default list argument is created once at function-definition time and shared across every call that doesn't pass target explicitly - classic Python mutable-default-argument bug. Verified directly: append_item(1) then append_item(2) returns [1, 2] for the second call, not [2].
diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/appender.py
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+def append_item(item, target=[]):
+    target.append(item)
+    return target
